headline: BARKLY RARE EARTHS LIFTS RESOURCE FIVE-FOLD TO 205 MT — A Third of Total in Critical Magnet-Grade Oxides
snippet: ASX-listed Barkly Rare Earths reported a five-fold increase in its inferred resource to 205 million tonnes at 2,100 ppm total rare earth oxides, with approximately one-third classified as magnet-grade oxides critical for EV motors and defence applications. The upgrade marks one of the largest rare earth resource announcements from an ASX junior in 2026, arriving as China's export controls keep Western buyers scrambling for non-Chinese supply.

headline: SILVER FUTURES JUMP 10% AS SHORT SELLERS FLEE — What Drove the Thanksgiving Short Squeeze
snippet: Silver futures surged more than 10% and gold reclaimed $3,600 on Friday as short sellers who had pushed silver near $38 two days earlier scrambled to cover on holiday-thin North American volume. Coinpaper's analysis identifies the move as a classic short-squeeze dynamic rather than a fundamental shift, with the gold-silver ratio still at 83 — historically cheap for silver — and Wednesday's selloff to $38 described as the extreme that set up the snapback.

headline: THAILAND MOVES TO BLOCK CHEMICALS FUELING MYANMAR RARE EARTH MINES — Toxic Metals Found in Downstream Rivers
snippet: Thailand's deputy prime minister announced plans to restrict exports of chemicals used in rare earth mining operations in Myanmar after toxic metals were detected in Thai rivers downstream from the mines. Reuters reported Thailand aims to present Myanmar with conclusive pollution evidence by January 2027. Analysts say the supply impact is unclear until specific chemicals and enforcement timelines emerge, but Myanmar is a significant supplier of heavy rare earth elements, and any supply disruption would tighten an already stressed non-Chinese market.

headline: HAYASA METALS WRAPS 2026 URASAR DRILLING — Strong Porphyry Alteration Confirmed but Grades Still Low (TSXV: HAY)
snippet: Hayasa Metals (TSX-V: HAY) reported its final 2026 drill results at the Urasar project in northern Armenia, with both holes confirming strong to intense hydrothermal alteration and stockwork veining consistent with the upper levels of a porphyry copper-gold system. Copper and gold grades remained low, however, indicating the mineralized core has not yet been intersected. Management released an updated strategic focus alongside the results, suggesting a rethink of drill targeting methodology before the next program.

headline: COPPER LOGS WORST MONTH SINCE 2022 WITH 18% NOVEMBER DECLINE — Violent Short-Cover Bounce Doesn't Change the Thesis
snippet: Copper's November 2026 decline reached approximately 18% before a sharp short-covering rally on Friday lifted LME prices in the biggest single-day copper move since January, according to Mining.com. The monthly slump is the worst since 2022 and was driven by new U.S. tariffs, rising rate expectations, and softening AI infrastructure spend forecasts. JPMorgan maintained a cautious $11,000-per-tonne 2027 price target, calling the Friday recovery fragile.

headline: LITHIUM HITS 2026 YEAR LOW AT $12.90/KG — Data Centre Demand Surge Fails to Rescue Oversupplied Market
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices hit their lowest level of 2026 at approximately USD $12.90/kg, according to the CHF Capital weekly roundup. Despite growing demand for energy storage at data centres, persistent oversupply from new Australian and South American hard-rock capacity is keeping prices suppressed. The year-low leaves most junior lithium developers unable to justify project economics at current prices, adding pressure on names that raised capital in 2024-25 at far higher price assumptions.

headline: WHO HAS A CUSHION? Investing.com Maps Gold/Silver Miners at 15-Month Stock Lows
snippet: An Investing.com analysis maps which gold and silver producers are most vulnerable at current 15-month equity lows — with the sector down 29–49% while the gold price is down approximately 26% over three months. The piece identifies producers facing analyst estimate cuts, including Barrick, Agnico Eagle, and Kinross, while distinguishing companies whose cash flows and balance sheets can survive a prolonged price correction. Balance sheet strength and low all-in sustaining costs are cited as the two most predictive factors for which names recover first.

headline: GOLD DOESN'T PAY DIVIDENDS? THESE 3 DO — Barrick Leads at 1.79% But Watch the Variable Payout Risk
snippet: A 24/7 Wall St. analysis highlights three gold mining stocks generating real dividend income as an alternative to holding bullion, led by Barrick Gold at a 1.79% yield. The piece warns that Barrick's variable top-up dividend is directly linked to quarterly gold prices, creating significant payout volatility during the current correction, and flags its exposure to Mali, the DRC, and Pakistan as geopolitical risks that make the yield less predictable than it appears on a screener.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR ENERGY TABLES ALL-STOCK BID FOR NOBLE PLAINS URANIUM AT NEAR-DOUBLE PREMIUM (TSXV)
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy signed a binding letter of intent to acquire all outstanding shares of TSX-V-listed Noble Plains Uranium in an all-stock transaction, offering C$0.125 per share — nearly double Noble Plains' October 29, 2026 closing price of C$0.065. The deal is structured as a plan of arrangement, suggesting Eagle Nuclear sees value in Noble Plains' uranium assets as spot prices hold near $90 per pound.

headline: ENERGY FUELS TARGETS 1 MILLION LBS URANIUM AT WHITE MESA MILL DEC-Q1 2027 — North America's Only Operating Conventional Mill
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE American: UUUU) announced plans to produce approximately one million pounds of finished uranium concentrate at its White Mesa Mill in Utah from December 2026 through the first quarter of 2027. White Mesa is the only conventional uranium mill currently operating in North America, giving Energy Fuels a production capacity advantage as spot uranium holds near $90 per pound. The announcement signals growing producer confidence that current prices justify ramping up output.
